_about: 60 raw items as they would arrive at a news desk in one working day, across 28 real events plus 8 items of noise. Written to read like genuine incoming copy. Every organisation and person named here is invented; only places (cities, districts, highways) are real.
_time_model: Offsets are hours relative to the moment `manage.py seeddesk` runs, so 'yesterday' is never empty for a reviewer opening the app next week. received_offset_hours is when the desk got it (this starts the dwell clock); published_offset_hours is the source's own timestamp.
_test_metadata: expected_event is ground truth for the clusterer tests only — the application never reads it. expected_noise marks items a reporter should spike.

_designed_cases.same-event-three-ways: event 'metro-purple-line-fault' arrives four times: wire copy, the transit corporation's own release, a commuter blog, and a social post. Must collapse to one story.
_designed_cases.lookalike-not-same-a: 'pharma-zydan-phase3' and 'pharma-verakine-phase3' — two different companies announcing Phase 3 topline data the same morning in near-identical press-release boilerplate. High lexical overlap, disjoint entities and quantities. Must stay separate.
_designed_cases.lookalike-not-same-b: 'nh48-palanpur-crash' and 'nh48-sirohi-crash' — two crashes on the same highway on the same day. Different districts, different tolls, six hours apart. Must stay separate.
_designed_cases.post-publish-merge: 'vizhinjam-offshore-firm' and 'coastal-logistics-response' share no entities at first, so they correctly do not cluster and both get published. The late-arriving item in 'vizhinjam-offshore-firm' (mw-0412) ties them together, and the editor merges after publication.
_designed_cases.near-miss-same-org: 'metro-fare-revision' is about the same transit corporation and city as 'metro-purple-line-fault' but is a different story three days earlier — the time signal is what has to separate them.

items.headline: Purple Line metro services disrupted for over four hours after cable fault in Bengaluru
items.body:
BENGALURU: Metro services on Bengaluru's Purple Line were suspended between Indiranagar and Byappanahalli for more than four hours on Tuesday morning after a fault in the overhead power cable, stranding commuters at six stations during peak hours.

Bengaluru Urban Transit Corporation said the fault was detected at 8.12 am near Halasuru and that trains were held at the nearest platforms as a precaution. Services on the affected stretch resumed at 12.40 pm after repair crews replaced a 40-metre section of overhead equipment.

A BUTC spokesperson, Anitha Raghavan, said about 60,000 commuters were affected and that feeder buses were pressed into service on the corridor. The corporation has ordered an internal review of its cable maintenance schedule.

items.headline: BUTC restores Purple Line services after overhead equipment repair
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Bengaluru Urban Transit Corporation (BUTC) wishes to inform commuters that normal train operations on the Purple Line between Indiranagar and Byappanahalli were restored at 12.40 pm today, following the successful replacement of a damaged section of overhead equipment near Halasuru station.

The fault was identified at 8.12 am during routine monitoring. In line with standard safety protocol, trains on the affected stretch were held at the nearest station and passengers were detrained in an orderly manner. Short-loop services continued on the remaining sections of the corridor throughout the morning.

BUTC deployed 42 feeder buses along the affected stretch and waived exit charges at four stations. The Corporation regrets the inconvenience caused to approximately 60,000 commuters and has constituted an internal committee to review overhead equipment inspection intervals.

For media queries: Anitha Raghavan, General Manager (Corporate Communications).

items.headline: Four hours on a platform: what Tuesday's Purple Line failure looked like from Indiranagar
items.body:
I got to Indiranagar at 8.20 am and the indicator board was already frozen on the same train that never came. By 8.45 the platform was three deep. Staff were doing their best but nobody had been told anything they could repeat, so the announcements just cycled between 'technical issue' and 'shortly'. The gates opened around 9.15 to let people out without paying again, which was the one thing that clearly went right.

What you don't see in the press note is what happened on the road outside. The feeder buses arrived, eventually, but the Old Madras Road stretch was already gridlocked by then, so the bus was slower than walking to Halasuru. I know people who gave up and paid ₹480 for an eight-kilometre auto ride.

This is the third overhead equipment failure on this corridor since February. At some point 'we have constituted a committee' stops being an answer.

items.headline: Zydan Therapeutics reports positive topline Phase 3 results for oral migraine candidate ZT-441
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

HYDERABAD — Zydan Therapeutics today announced positive topline results from ASCEND-3, its pivotal Phase 3 trial of ZT-441, an investigational oral calcitonin gene-related peptide antagonist for the acute treatment of migraine.

The trial met its primary endpoint, with 31.4% of patients receiving ZT-441 achieving freedom from pain at two hours versus 18.9% on placebo (p<0.001). The study enrolled 1,142 adults across 74 sites. ZT-441 was generally well tolerated; the most common adverse events were nausea (4.1%) and somnolence (2.8%), and discontinuation rates were comparable to placebo.

'These data support ZT-441 as a potential new option for patients who cannot tolerate existing acute therapies,' said Dr Meera Sundaram, Chief Medical Officer at Zydan Therapeutics. The company intends to file a New Drug Application in the first half of next year.

This release contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied.

items.headline: Verakine Biosciences announces Phase 3 topline data for once-daily hypertension candidate VK-208
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

PUNE — Verakine Biosciences today announced topline results from HORIZON-2, its Phase 3 study evaluating VK-208, a once-daily investigational aldosterone synthase inhibitor, in adults with uncontrolled hypertension.

The study met its primary endpoint. Patients receiving VK-208 showed a placebo-adjusted reduction in mean 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure of 8.6 mmHg at week 12 (p<0.001). A total of 806 patients were randomised across 51 centres. VK-208 was generally well tolerated, with hyperkalaemia reported in 2.2% of the treatment arm versus 0.9% on placebo.

'Roughly half of all treated hypertensive patients remain above target, and this result speaks directly to that gap,' said Dr Arvind Kelkar, Head of Clinical Development at Verakine Biosciences. Full results will be presented at a scientific congress later this year.

This release contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied.

items.headline: Four killed as truck rams stationary bus on NH-48 near Palanpur
items.body:
PALANPUR: Four people were killed and eleven injured when a container truck rammed into a stationary private bus on National Highway 48 near Palanpur in Banaskantha district early on Tuesday, police said.

The bus had pulled onto the shoulder after a tyre burst at around 5.40 am when the truck, travelling towards Ahmedabad, hit it from behind, Banaskantha district police said. Three of the dead were passengers seated in the rear of the bus; the fourth was the bus conductor. The injured were taken to the civil hospital at Palanpur, where two are described as critical.

The truck driver fled the scene and a search is under way. Traffic on the Ahmedabad-bound carriageway was diverted for about two hours.

items.headline: Three dead in car-tempo collision on NH-48 in Rajasthan's Sirohi
items.body:
SIROHI: Three members of a family were killed when the car they were travelling in collided head-on with a goods tempo on National Highway 48 in Rajasthan's Sirohi district on Tuesday afternoon, police said.

The collision occurred near Swaroopganj at about 11.50 am when the tempo, which was carrying cement, veered across the median, Sirohi police said. The deceased were residents of Udaipur returning from Mount Abu. Two others in the car, including a child, were injured and admitted to a hospital in Abu Road.

The tempo driver has been detained and a case registered.

items.headline: Leaked filings name a Mauritius-registered firm in the Vizhinjam port equipment contract
items.body:
A set of corporate filings shared with this publication shows that a Mauritius-registered company received ₹2,400 crore in payments linked to the crane and gantry package for the Vizhinjam port expansion between 2023 and last year.

The filings, which appear to be internal reconciliation statements prepared for an audit, identify the recipient only by a registration number and the description 'offshore equipment counterparty'. That number resolves, in the Mauritius companies registry, to an entity incorporated in 2021 whose registered office is shared with fourteen other companies.

We have not been able to establish who controls the entity. Two people with knowledge of the tender, who asked not to be named because the audit is ongoing, said the equipment package was awarded without a competing technical bid. The Port Trust did not respond to a detailed questionnaire sent on Friday.

items.headline: Coastal Logistics Group says it has always complied with disclosure norms
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

KOCHI — Coastal Logistics Group has taken note of a report published today concerning payments associated with port equipment procurement.

The Group states that all payments made by it and by its subsidiaries are recorded in its audited financial statements and have been disclosed to the relevant authorities in accordance with applicable law. The Group has at all times complied with disclosure norms and with the terms of every contract to which it is a party.

The Group will not comment on documents whose provenance it cannot verify, and reserves its rights in respect of any inaccurate reporting. Coastal Logistics Group remains committed to the highest standards of corporate governance.

Media contact: Priya Menon, Vice President (Communications).

items.headline: Mauritius firm named in leaked Vizhinjam filings is a Coastal Logistics subsidiary, registry documents show
items.body:
KOCHI: The Mauritius-registered company identified in leaked reconciliation filings as the recipient of ₹2,400 crore in payments for port equipment at Vizhinjam is Arvent Holdings Ltd, and it is an indirect subsidiary of Coastal Logistics Group, according to registry documents reviewed by Meridian Wire.

Arvent Holdings' 2024 annual return lists its sole shareholder as a Singapore entity, Bellhaven Pte Ltd, whose own director filings name two serving officers of Coastal Logistics Group.

Coastal Logistics said in a statement earlier this week that all payments by the Group and its subsidiaries were recorded in its audited accounts and disclosed to authorities. That statement did not name Arvent Holdings. Asked about the shareholding chain on Tuesday, a Coastal Logistics spokesperson said the Group had 'nothing to add to its earlier statement'. The Port Trust declined to comment.

items.headline: Cabinet clears ₹18,600-crore incentive for two semiconductor fabrication units
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

NEW DELHI — The Union Cabinet has approved an outlay of ₹18,600 crore under the Semiconductor Manufacturing Incentive Scheme for the establishment of two fabrication units, one in Gujarat and one in Karnataka.

The Gujarat unit will have an installed capacity of 40,000 wafer starts per month at the 28-nanometre node. The Karnataka unit will focus on compound semiconductors for automotive and power applications. Together the two projects represent committed private investment of ₹76,000 crore and are expected to create 4,300 direct jobs.

Disbursement will be linked to construction and production milestones verified by an independent agency. Commercial production at the Gujarat unit is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028.

items.headline: Cabinet approves ₹18,600 crore for two chip fabs; commercial output targeted for 2028
items.body:
NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved incentives worth ₹18,600 crore for two semiconductor fabrication plants, in Gujarat and Karnataka, the Ministry of Industry & Commerce said.

The Gujarat facility is planned at 40,000 wafer starts a month on the 28nm node, while the Karnataka plant will make compound semiconductors for automotive and power electronics. The ministry put committed private investment across the two projects at ₹76,000 crore and direct employment at 4,300.

Industry executives said the 28nm choice was pragmatic rather than headline-grabbing, since that node still accounts for a large share of automotive and industrial demand. Payouts are tied to milestones certified by an independent agency, a condition added after slippage in an earlier round of the scheme.

items.headline: Orange alert for Mumbai, Thane and Raigad; 200 mm rainfall likely in 24 hours
items.body:
BULLETIN NO. 214

The National Weather Bureau has placed Mumbai, Thane and Raigad districts under an orange alert for the next 24 hours. Extremely heavy rainfall of 150 to 200 mm is likely at isolated places, accompanied by gusty winds of 45 to 55 kmph along the coast.

A low pressure area over the north-east Arabian Sea is expected to intensify over the next 12 hours before moving north-north-east. Fishermen are advised not to venture into the sea off the Maharashtra and Gujarat coasts until Thursday morning.

A high tide of 4.6 metres is expected at 1.42 pm. Residents of low-lying areas are advised to avoid non-essential travel.

items.headline: Mumbai under orange alert as weather bureau forecasts up to 200 mm rain in a day
items.body:
MUMBAI: The National Weather Bureau issued an orange alert for Mumbai, Thane and Raigad on Tuesday, forecasting extremely heavy rainfall of 150 to 200 mm at isolated places over the next 24 hours.

The civic body said 187 pumps had been positioned at chronic flooding points and that the disaster management cell would run through the night. Suburban services on the Western line were running six to nine minutes late by mid-afternoon. Schools in Mumbai and Thane will remain shut on Wednesday, the municipal commissioner said.

The bureau linked the spell to a low pressure area over the north-east Arabian Sea and warned of a 4.6-metre high tide at 1.42 pm, which typically slows drainage in low-lying wards.

items.headline: Urban unemployment rate at 6.4% in the July-September quarter, says statistics office
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

NEW DELHI — The National Statistics Office today released the quarterly bulletin of the Periodic Labour Force Survey for July-September. The unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above in urban areas stood at 6.4%, compared with 6.6% in the preceding quarter and 6.9% in the same quarter a year earlier.

The labour force participation rate in urban areas rose to 51.2% from 50.8%. The worker population ratio was 47.9%. Female labour force participation in urban areas was recorded at 26.1%, an increase of 0.7 percentage points over the previous quarter.

The survey covered 44,286 urban households across all states and union territories. Detailed tables are available in the bulletin annexure.

items.headline: Urban joblessness eases to 6.4%; female participation up to 26.1%
items.body:
NEW DELHI: Urban unemployment fell to 6.4% in the July-September quarter from 6.6% in the previous three months, the National Statistics Office said on Tuesday, while urban female labour force participation rose to 26.1%.

The labour force participation rate for urban Indians aged 15 and above rose to 51.2% from 50.8%, and the worker population ratio was 47.9%. The survey covered 44,286 urban households.

Economists cautioned against reading a trend into a single quarter. 'A 0.2 point move is inside the noise band for a survey this size, and the participation number is the more interesting one,' said Kavitha Nandagopal, an economist who studies labour data. She said the female participation increase, if sustained over two more quarters, would be the first durable improvement since the series was revised.

items.headline: Sundara Finance Bank posts Q2 net profit of ₹1,842 crore, up 14.6% year on year
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

MUMBAI — Sundara Finance Bank today reported a net profit of ₹1,842 crore for the quarter ended September, an increase of 14.6% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

Net interest income grew 11.2% to ₹4,318 crore. The net interest margin stood at 3.94%, compared with 4.06% a year earlier. Gross non-performing assets improved to 2.11% of gross advances from 2.38%, and net NPAs stood at 0.54%. The provision coverage ratio was 78.4%.

Advances grew 15.8% year on year to ₹4.21 lakh crore, led by the retail and MSME segments. Deposits grew 13.1% to ₹5.06 lakh crore, with CASA at 41.7%. The capital adequacy ratio under Basel III stood at 17.2%.

items.headline: Sundara Finance Bank Q2 profit rises 14.6% to ₹1,842 crore; margin narrows to 3.94%
items.body:
MUMBAI: Sundara Finance Bank reported a 14.6% rise in second-quarter net profit to ₹1,842 crore on Tuesday, but its net interest margin narrowed to 3.94% from 4.06% a year earlier as deposit costs continued to bite.

Net interest income rose 11.2% to ₹4,318 crore. Gross bad loans improved to 2.11% of advances from 2.38%. Advances grew 15.8% to ₹4.21 lakh crore while deposits grew 13.1% to ₹5.06 lakh crore, leaving the bank's credit-deposit ratio a little tighter than a year ago.

The margin compression is the number analysts had flagged going into the quarter. On a call with analysts, management guided to margins stabilising 'in the region of 3.9%' over the second half.

items.headline: Kelpie lays off 180, closes its Jakarta and Manila teams
items.body:
Kelpie, the logistics-software company that raised a $54 million Series C fourteen months ago, cut 180 roles on Monday and shut its Jakarta and Manila offices entirely. That is roughly 22% of headcount.

Three people affected told me the cuts landed by calendar invite at 7.30 am local time, with a company-wide call thirty minutes later. Severance is two months plus one week per year of service, and the company is paying out notice in the two closing offices rather than requiring notice periods to be worked.

The pattern here is familiar: a Series C raised against a growth plan for Southeast Asia, an enterprise sales cycle that turned out to be nine months rather than four, and a board that would rather see eighteen months of runway than a second bridge round. Kelpie's founder said on the call that the company is now 'default alive'. Two of the three people I spoke to used the phrase 'too late' about the Manila closure specifically.

items.headline: Logistics software firm Kelpie cuts 180 jobs, exits Southeast Asia
items.body:
BENGALURU: Kelpie, a logistics software company, has cut 180 jobs and closed its offices in Jakarta and Manila, the company confirmed on Tuesday. The reduction amounts to about 22% of its workforce.

Affected employees will receive two months' severance plus one week of pay for each year of service, a company spokesperson said. Kelpie raised $54 million in a Series C round fourteen months ago.

'We built for a Southeast Asia ramp that did not arrive on the timeline we planned for,' founder and chief executive Rohan Dias said in a statement. The company said it would continue to serve existing customers in the region from Bengaluru.

items.headline: Second Test: hosts reach 287 for 4 at stumps on day one after Fernandes century
items.body:
CHENNAI: Opener Neil Fernandes made 118 as the hosts closed the first day of the second Test on 287 for 4, having chosen to bat on a surface that offered turn from the fortieth over onwards.

Fernandes faced 194 balls and hit fourteen fours before being caught at short cover shortly after tea. He put on 141 for the second wicket with Vikram Ahuja, who was unbeaten on 76 at the close. The visitors' spinners took three of the four wickets to fall.

The hosts lead the three-match series 1-0.

items.headline: Delhi air quality slips to 'severe'; construction curbs under GRAP Stage III come into force
items.body:
NEW DELHI: Delhi's 24-hour average air quality index touched 412 on Tuesday morning, in the 'severe' band, and Stage III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan came into force across the National Capital Region from 8 am.

The measures bar non-essential construction and demolition, close stone crushers and mining, and restrict the entry of older commercial vehicles. Primary schools in Delhi will move to online classes from Wednesday.

The worst readings were recorded at Anand Vihar (438) and Wazirpur (429). Calm surface winds and a shallow mixing layer are expected to keep concentrations high until Thursday, when a western disturbance may bring some relief.

items.headline: Air quality bulletin: calm winds to keep NCR concentrations in the severe band until Thursday
items.body:
BULLETIN NO. 211

The 24-hour average AQI for Delhi at 0700 hours was 412 (severe). Station maxima were recorded at Anand Vihar (438) and Wazirpur (429).

Surface winds are calm to light (4-8 kmph) with a mixing layer depth of approximately 800 metres, which is unfavourable for dispersion. These conditions are expected to persist through Wednesday. A western disturbance approaching from the north-west may improve ventilation from Thursday afternoon.

Predominant contributors over the last 24 hours were transport (17%), stubble burning (14%) and dust (12%).

items.headline: Fire at garment unit in Tirupur; no casualties, seven workers treated for smoke inhalation
items.body:
PRESS NOTE

A fire was reported at a garment processing unit in the Mannarai industrial area of Tirupur at 2.10 am today. Six fire tenders from Tirupur and Palladam responded and the fire was brought under control by 4.35 am.

There were no casualties. Seven workers who were present on the night shift were treated for smoke inhalation at a private hospital and six have since been discharged. The unit's dyeing section and a bale storage area were destroyed.

A preliminary examination indicates an electrical short circuit in the dyeing section. A case has been registered and the Electrical Inspectorate has been asked to examine the premises.

— District Police, Public Relations Office

items.headline: Seven treated after fire guts dyeing section of Tirupur garment unit
items.body:
TIRUPUR: A fire destroyed the dyeing section and a bale storage area of a garment processing unit in Tirupur's Mannarai industrial area early on Tuesday, police said. Seven workers on the night shift were treated for smoke inhalation and six have been discharged.

Six fire tenders brought the blaze under control by 4.35 am, about two hours and twenty-five minutes after it was reported. Police said a preliminary examination pointed to an electrical short circuit in the dyeing section and that the Electrical Inspectorate had been asked to inspect the premises.

Tirupur's processing units have been the subject of repeated safety notices; the district administration said 14 units were issued directions in the last quarter.

items.headline: Monetary Policy Committee keeps the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.25%
items.body:
STATEMENT OF THE MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE

The Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Monetary Authority, at its meeting concluded today, decided by a vote of four to two to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.25%. The standing deposit facility rate remains at 6.00% and the marginal standing facility rate at 6.50%.

The Committee retained its stance of withdrawal of accommodation. Headline retail inflation for the last reported month was 4.9%, with food inflation at 6.3%. The Committee projects inflation at 4.6% for the current financial year and real GDP growth at 6.8%.

Two members voted for a reduction of 25 basis points. The minutes of the meeting will be published on the fourteenth day from today.

items.headline: Repo rate held at 6.25% in a 4-2 vote; inflation projected at 4.6%
items.body:
MUMBAI: The Monetary Policy Committee kept the policy repo rate unchanged at 6.25% on Monday in a four-to-two vote, retaining its stance of withdrawal of accommodation, the Reserve Monetary Authority said.

The committee projected retail inflation at 4.6% for the current financial year and real GDP growth at 6.8%. Headline inflation in the last reported month was 4.9%, with food inflation at 6.3%.

The two dissenting votes, for a 25 basis point cut, are one more than at the previous meeting. Bond markets read the split as the more informative signal: the ten-year yield eased three basis points after the statement.

items.headline: Class 12 board examination date sheet released; examinations from February 17
items.body:
NOTICE NO. 214/EXAM

The State Board of Secondary Education has released the date sheet for the Class 12 examinations. Examinations will be conducted from 17 February to 21 March. The Class 10 examinations will be held from 20 February to 12 March.

Examinations will be held in a single shift from 10.30 am to 1.30 pm. Candidates must reach their examination centre by 10.00 am. A gap of at least one day has been provided between major subject papers.

Approximately 11.4 lakh candidates are expected to appear across 2,860 centres. The date sheet is available on the Board's website. Schools are directed to display this notice on their noticeboards by Friday.

items.headline: Depression over the Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Thursday
items.body:
BULLETIN NO. 208

The depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal moved north-westwards at 12 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred at 0530 hours about 620 km south-east of Visakhapatnam.

It is very likely to intensify into a deep depression by Wednesday morning and further into a cyclonic storm by Thursday morning, while continuing to move north-westwards. Squally winds reaching 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph are likely over the west-central Bay from Wednesday.

Fishermen are advised not to venture into the east-central and west-central Bay of Bengal until further notice. Port authorities at Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam have been advised to hoist appropriate signals.

items.headline: State transport corporation floats tender for 1,500 electric buses on gross cost contract
items.body:
HYDERABAD: The state road transport corporation has invited bids for the procurement and twelve-year operation of 1,500 electric buses on a gross cost contract basis, under which operators are paid a per-kilometre rate and the corporation retains fare revenue.

The tender covers 900 twelve-metre and 600 nine-metre buses, to be deployed across five cities. Bidders must demonstrate prior operation of at least 200 electric buses. Charging infrastructure is the operator's responsibility, with depot land provided by the corporation on a nominal lease.

The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for the twenty-first and bids close on 8 December. The corporation currently operates 412 electric buses.

items.headline: Three days into the fee protest at the state university, nobody in the administration will say who set the figure
items.body:
The hostel fee revision that students have been sitting outside the administrative block over since Saturday is a 38% increase, from ₹2,900 to ₹4,000 a semester. That much everyone agrees on.

What nobody will say on the record is who decided it. The registrar's office says the finance committee approved it in August. Two members of the finance committee told me the item was tabled as 'revision of hostel charges as per norms', with no figure attached. The minutes, which are supposed to be published within thirty days, are not on the website.

About 400 students were at the block on Monday evening, down from perhaps 900 on Saturday. The vice-chancellor's office has offered a meeting on Thursday. Students want the revision stayed first. Both positions are reasonable and neither is moving.

items.headline: Dengue cases in the city cross 4,100 this season, up 62% on last year
items.body:
PUNE: The municipal health department has recorded 4,127 dengue cases this season, up 62% from 2,548 in the corresponding period last year, with nine deaths attributed to the disease.

The department said 218 cases were reported in the past week alone. Fogging has been carried out in 41 wards and 9,400 premises inspected for breeding sites, with notices issued to 612 property owners.

Doctors at two civic hospitals said this season's case mix includes a higher proportion of patients with low platelet counts requiring admission. Health officials attributed the rise to intermittent late-season rainfall, which leaves standing water at construction sites and on terraces without triggering the drainage that heavy continuous rain does.

items.headline: Installed solar capacity crosses 120 GW; rooftop segment adds 3.4 GW in the quarter
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

NEW DELHI — Cumulative installed solar capacity has crossed 120 GW, the Department of Renewable Energy said today. Utility-scale projects account for 96.8 GW and rooftop and distributed installations for 23.4 GW.

The rooftop segment added 3.4 GW during the July-September quarter, its highest quarterly addition, taking the residential rooftop programme past 1.9 million households. Module manufacturing capacity in the country now stands at 78 GW annually and cell capacity at 26 GW.

The Department said 14.2 GW of utility-scale capacity awarded in earlier tranches remains unconstructed on account of transmission connectivity delays, and that a coordination mechanism with the transmission utility has been set up.

items.headline: BUTC submits fare revision proposal to the Fare Fixation Committee
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Bengaluru Urban Transit Corporation (BUTC) has submitted a fare revision proposal to the Fare Fixation Committee for its consideration. The proposal, if accepted, would revise the minimum fare from ₹10 to ₹12 and the maximum fare from ₹60 to ₹70.

BUTC has proposed that fares for journeys of up to four kilometres remain unchanged, and that the existing 5% discount on smart card journeys be raised to 10% to encourage cashless travel. Concessional fares for students and senior citizens are proposed to be retained without change.

Fares on the network were last revised in 2021. The Corporation's operating ratio for the last financial year was 1.34. The Committee is expected to hold public consultations before submitting its recommendations.

items.headline: Monthly GST collections at ₹1.87 lakh crore, up 8.9% year on year
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

NEW DELHI — Gross Goods and Services Tax revenue for the month was ₹1.87 lakh crore, an increase of 8.9% over the same month last year.

Of this, Central GST accounted for ₹34,200 crore, State GST for ₹42,600 crore, Integrated GST for ₹96,100 crore including ₹49,300 crore collected on imports, and cess for ₹13,800 crore. Refunds of ₹22,400 crore were issued during the month, making net revenue ₹1.65 lakh crore.

Domestic transactions grew 7.6% and revenue from the import of goods grew 12.1%. Fourteen states recorded growth above the national average.

items.headline: GST collections rise 8.9% to ₹1.87 lakh crore; import component grows fastest
items.body:
NEW DELHI: Gross GST collections rose 8.9% year on year to ₹1.87 lakh crore last month, with revenue from imported goods growing 12.1% against 7.6% for domestic transactions, the Ministry of Industry & Commerce said.

Net of ₹22,400 crore in refunds, revenue was ₹1.65 lakh crore. Integrated GST accounted for ₹96,100 crore, of which ₹49,300 crore came from imports.

The gap between the import and domestic growth rates is the line worth watching: it has widened for three consecutive months, which economists read as import demand running ahead of domestic consumption rather than as a compliance effect.

items.headline: Vayu Air to add 11 routes from Bhubaneswar and Coimbatore from December
items.body:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

GURUGRAM — Vayu Air today announced the addition of eleven routes from Bhubaneswar and Coimbatore, to be introduced in phases from 4 December.

Bhubaneswar will receive new daily services to Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Nagpur, Varanasi and Guwahati. Coimbatore will receive daily services to Pune, Jaipur, Kolkata and Visakhapatnam, and double daily services to Hyderabad. The routes will be operated with the airline's 180-seat narrow-body fleet.

With these additions Vayu Air will serve 74 destinations and operate 612 daily departures. Bookings open today across all channels.

items.headline: Vayu Air adds 11 routes from Bhubaneswar and Coimbatore in tier-two push
items.body:
NEW DELHI: Vayu Air will add eleven routes from Bhubaneswar and Coimbatore from 4 December, taking its network to 74 destinations and 612 daily departures, the airline said on Tuesday.

Five of the new routes originate at Bhubaneswar and six at Coimbatore, all operated with 180-seat narrow-body aircraft. Nine of the eleven are routes on which no carrier currently offers a direct service.

The expansion continues a pattern across Indian carriers of adding metro-to-tier-two capacity where slot constraints at the largest airports do not bind. Vayu Air's load factor for the last reported month was 87.4%.

items.headline: The waste-to-energy plant hearing lasted 40 minutes and took no questions
items.body:
The public hearing for the 11-megawatt waste-to-energy plant proposed at Mavallipura was scheduled for two hours. It ran for forty minutes.

The project proponent presented for twenty-two minutes. The environmental consultant read the mitigation section of the impact assessment for eleven. Then the presiding officer said written objections would be accepted for thirty days and closed the hearing. Roughly 200 residents had come; perhaps six got to speak.

The substantive objection, which did get raised, is about the feedstock assumption. The assessment assumes 600 tonnes per day of segregated combustible waste. The city's own quarterly figures put segregated dry waste collection at 340 tonnes per day across all wards. Nobody from the corporation was on the panel to answer where the other 260 tonnes are meant to come from.

items.headline: Residents object to feedstock assumptions at waste-to-energy plant hearing in Bengaluru
items.body:
BENGALURU: A public hearing on a proposed 11 MW waste-to-energy plant at Mavallipura was closed after forty minutes on Tuesday, with residents objecting that the project's feedstock assumptions do not match the city's segregated waste collection figures.

The environmental impact assessment assumes 600 tonnes per day of segregated combustible waste. Municipal figures for the last quarter put segregated dry waste collection at 340 tonnes per day. The presiding officer said written objections would be received for thirty days.

About 200 residents attended. A representative of the project proponent said the feedstock question would be addressed in the written response.

items.headline: 'Kaandhal Nadi' holds 71% of its opening weekend in week two — the number nobody predicted
items.body:
The second weekend for 'Kaandhal Nadi' came in at ₹18.4 crore against an opening weekend of ₹25.9 crore. A 71% hold in week two is not a normal number for a film with no star in the lead and a 152-minute runtime.

The distribution read is that the film is doing something unusual in single screens in tier-two centres, where it is holding above 60% occupancy in evening shows three weekends in. The multiplex chains have been adding shows rather than cutting them, which is the tell.

Total is now ₹61.2 crore worldwide against a production budget widely reported at ₹14 crore. The interesting question for the trade is not this film; it is whether the two similar mid-budget films dated for December get their screen counts revised upward.

items.headline: Teenager wins Candidates qualifier on tiebreak to secure world championship cycle place
items.body:
ASTANA: Seventeen-year-old Aditi Raman won the Candidates qualifier on tiebreak on Tuesday, after her closest rival drew from a winning position in the final round, securing a place in the next world championship cycle.

Raman finished on 8.5 points from eleven games, level with two others, and took the place on a superior direct-encounter score. She was unbeaten across the event, with six wins and five draws.

She becomes the youngest player to qualify from this event.

items.headline: Port workers' unions serve notice for a three-day strike from the 18th over contract labour
items.body:
KOCHI: Four port workers' unions have served notice for a three-day strike from the eighteenth at three major ports, over the engagement of contract labour in cargo handling operations.

The unions say 1,840 posts across the three ports have been kept vacant and the work assigned to contractors at lower rates. A conciliation meeting convened by the regional labour commissioner on Monday ended without agreement.

Port authorities said contingency arrangements were being drawn up. The three ports together handled 41.6 million tonnes of cargo in the last financial year.

items.headline: Vigilance registers case over 2021 ventilator purchase; 240 units still uninstalled
items.body:
BHOPAL: The state vigilance directorate has registered a case in connection with the purchase of 900 ventilators in 2021, of which 240 remain uninstalled in district hospital stores, officials said.

The first information report names three officials of the health services directorate and two firms. It alleges that technical specifications were altered after the pre-bid meeting in a manner that narrowed eligibility, and that units were accepted without the third-party inspection the contract required.

The purchase order value was ₹78 crore. A departmental audit last year had flagged the uninstalled units; the vigilance case follows a reference from that audit.

items.headline: Tiger numbers in the reserve rise to 84 from 71 in the last all-India estimation
items.body:
NAGPUR: The tiger population in the reserve has risen to 84 from 71 at the last all-India estimation four years ago, according to figures released by the field director's office.

The estimate is based on 1,240 camera trap locations covering 2,860 square kilometres over 62 days, with 41 individual tigers photo-captured in the core area. The reserve recorded 19 cubs during the period.

Human-wildlife conflict compensation claims in the buffer zone rose to 1,412 from 980 over the same period, and the field director's office said a review of the compensation process had been ordered.
